clauses: The argument is a dictionary with exactly n, days, supply, demand, carry_capacity, storage_cost, and transfers; all numeric fields are integers, not booleans.
There are n locations, with 1 <= n <= 2, and days dates numbered 0 through days-1, with 1 <= days <= 3.
Supply and demand are days-by-n lists of integers from 0 through 2; every supply unit must be used and every demand unit must be satisfied at its specified location and date.
Carry_capacity and storage_cost are (days-1)-by-n lists; each capacity is 0 through 2 and each cost is -3 through 3.
A carry flow at location p from date d to date d+1 is an integer between zero and carry_capacity[d][p], and costs storage_cost[d][p] per unit.

Transfers contains zero through three lists [date, u, v, capacity, cost], with valid date and location indices, capacity 0 through 2, and cost -3 through 3; duplicates and self-loops are allowed and each entry has its own capacity.
A transfer sends an integer between zero and capacity units from u to v on its date at its cost per unit; incoming transfers may supply outgoing transfers on the same date, including circulations.

At each location and date, supply plus incoming transfers plus carry from the preceding date must equal demand plus outgoing transfers plus carry to the following date; there is no initial or final inventory beyond these flows and no disposal.
Return the minimum total carry and transfer cost as an integer, or None if the equalities cannot all be met.
Do not modify the argument or any nested object.
The argument is a dictionary with exactly the specified keys; all numeric fields are integers, not booleans.
The field n is between 1 and 4 and names vertices 0 through n-1; arcs is a list of zero through six lists [u, v, lower, upper, cost].
Each arc has endpoints in 0 through n-1, 0 <= lower <= upper <= 2, and -5 <= cost <= 5; parallel arcs and self-loops are allowed and list positions identify distinct arcs.
A feasible circulation assigns an integer flow to every arc between its inclusive lower and upper bounds, with total incoming flow equal to total outgoing flow at every vertex.
Its total cost is the sum over arcs of flow times cost; the optimum is the minimum total cost among feasible circulations, or None if none exists.
The dictionary keys are exactly n and arcs.
For each position i in arcs, form a separate scenario from the original arcs by setting both bounds of arc i to zero, even if its original lower bound was positive; retain every other bound and cost.
Return a new list of integers or None giving each separate scenario optimum in arc order; return an empty list when arcs is empty.
Do not modify the argument or any nested object.
The argument is a dictionary with exactly n, start, rules, budget, and text; all numeric fields are integers, not booleans.
There are n nonterminal symbols numbered 0 through n-1, where 1 <= n <= 3, and start is one of those symbols.
Rules is a list of zero through six lists [lhs, rhs, resource, cost], where lhs is a nonterminal, resource is 1 through 3, and cost is -5 through 5.
Each rhs is either an empty list, a one-element list containing the terminal string "a" or "b", a one-element list containing a nonterminal integer, or a two-element list of nonterminal integers.
Budget is between 0 and 16 inclusive; text is a string of zero through seven characters, all from "ab".

A derivation is a finite ordered tree rooted at start; every nonterminal occurrence chooses one rule with that lhs, and the rhs gives its ordered children, with an empty rhs producing the empty string.
A tree yield is its terminal leaves read left to right; its resource and cost are the respective sums of resource and cost over all rule occurrences, including empty and unary rules.
A permitted tree has total resource at most budget; a nonterminal root always needs a rule occurrence, so budget zero permits no tree.
Recursive rules, nullable cycles, unused nonterminals, and duplicate rule entries are allowed; positions in rules distinguish rule identities.
Return as an integer the number of permitted trees whose yield equals text exactly, reduced modulo 1000000007; return zero if there is no such tree.

Two trees are distinct if their ordered tree structures or the rule identity at any corresponding occurrence differ; identical duplicate entries still give distinct choices, and costs have no effect on counting.

Implement forked_store_observations(arg). Arg has exactly bindings and branches. Bindings is an ordered list of at most 6 distinct [name,expression] pairs evaluated sequentially from empty environment and store, with each binding seeing earlier bindings. Preserve the resulting lexical environment for all branches.

Branches is a list of 0 to 6 objects with exactly from and program. For branch index i, from is -1 or an integer in [0,i). Start that branch with a copy of the initial store when from is -1, otherwise a copy of the selected earlier branch's final store. Run its program in the initial lexical environment, independently of other branches. Return the ordered list of {'value': final integer, 'store': final integer list} observations. No branch changes the initial or earlier branch stores.

Use exact built-in JSON types; integers exclude booleans. Expressions are integers or the arrays specified here. Names are nonempty lowercase ASCII strings of at most 8 letters. All evaluation is deterministic, left to right, and must preserve the input argument.

Expression forms are ['var',name], ['let',name,value,body], ['fn',parameter,body], ['call',function,argument], ['seq',first,second], ['if',condition,then,else], ['add',left,right], ['sub',left,right], ['ref',value], ['get',cell], ['set',cell,value], ['snap'], and ['restore',snapshot,body]. No other forms occur. Integer literals are between -20 and 20.

A let evaluates value in the current environment, then body with that name bound to the resulting value. A function captures a copy of its current lexical name bindings. A call evaluates function then argument in the caller environment, then evaluates the captured body in its captured environment extended by its parameter. There is no recursion binding. A seq discards its first value. An if evaluates only the selected arm: then when its integer condition is nonzero, otherwise else. Add and sub operate on integers.

The store starts as an empty ordered list of integer cells. Ref evaluates its integer argument, appends a cell, and returns a cell handle with ID equal to the previous store length. Get reads a handle's cell; set evaluates handle then integer value, overwrites that cell, and returns the assigned integer. Handles alias by integer ID, including across captured environments. All allocated cells, even unreachable cells, are observable in ascending ID order.

Snap returns an immutable copy of the current entire store, without allocation. Restore first evaluates its snapshot expression, replaces the entire current store by that snapshot, then evaluates body in the same lexical environment. Restoring also resets the next allocation ID to the restored length. A preexisting handle denotes its numeric ID in the restored store; using it is valid only if that ID exists at access time. A later allocation may reuse a discarded ID. Closures and snapshots retain captured bindings or store contents independently of subsequent changes.

All supplied expressions are well scoped, terminate, and are dynamically well typed on every evaluated path: arithmetic and conditions use integers; ref and set store integers only; call uses a closure; restore uses a snapshot; get and set use existing cell IDs. Every final program result is an integer. Each argument contains at most 100 expression nodes in total (including unevaluated function bodies), nesting at most 18, at most 300 evaluated expression nodes per program run, at most 8 cells in any store, and all intermediate integers have absolute value at most 10000. No invalid-input behavior is required.

Implement bounded_store_equivalence(arg). Arg has exactly left, right, and domain. Left and right are expressions. Domain is an ascending list of 0 to 7 distinct integers between -10 and 10. For each domain value x, independently run each program starting with an empty store and the single lexical binding x to that integer. Programs are equivalent at x exactly when both their final integer values and entire final ordered stores agree.

Return exactly {'equivalent': boolean, 'different_inputs': list of integers}, where different_inputs contains all domain members at which the programs differ, in domain order, and equivalent is true exactly when that list is empty. Empty domains are equivalent.

Implement fleet_assignment_cost(arg). Arg additionally has vehicles, a list of 1 to 3 vehicle objects. Assign every request to exactly one vehicle and serve it entirely on that vehicle. Every vehicle, even one assigned no requests, must perform a feasible route from its start to end. Minimize the sum of all vehicle route costs. Return that integer minimum, or null if no assignment and schedule is feasible.

All values use exact built-in JSON types; integers exclude booleans. Preserve the input. Arg contains time, cost, requests and the additional fields stated below, with no others. Time and cost are square matrices of size N, 1 <= N <= 9; entries are integers from 0 to 20 with zero diagonals. Matrices are directed and need not satisfy a triangle inequality. Entries give direct travel duration and direct monetary cost; they are independent quantities.

Requests is an ordered list of 0 to 4 distinct request occurrences (identical objects still count separately). Each request has pick and drop node indices in [0,N), load in [1,3], pw and dw as [earliest,latest] service-start windows with integer 0 <= earliest <= latest <= 80, and ps and ds as pickup and delivery service durations in [0,5]. Only the reward contract additionally has reward, an integer from 0 to 30. Pickup and delivery nodes may coincide, including with vehicle endpoints.

Each vehicle object has exactly start, end (node indices), capacity (integer 1 to 5), release and deadline (integers with 0 <= release <= deadline <= 100). It starts empty at start at release, visits exactly one pickup and one delivery event for each request assigned to it, and finishes empty at end by deadline inclusive. Each pickup must precede its own delivery, even at identical nodes. No unassigned events, extra waypoint visits, request transfers, or split loads are allowed.

For each event, travel directly from the previous node, then start service at the maximum of arrival time and its window earliest. Start must be at most window latest inclusive. Waiting is permitted and has no monetary cost. Service finishes after ps or ds time units; the next trip starts then. Load changes by +load at pickup and -load at delivery and must stay between zero and capacity inclusive. Finish time includes direct travel from the last event to end; an empty route travels directly from start to end. Extra waiting cannot improve feasibility and is allowed only if all these constraints remain satisfied.

Route monetary cost is the sum of cost entries for every traveled leg, including the initial leg and the final leg to end, and excluding waiting and service durations. A correct return uses an integer optimum, or null exactly where specified. No invalid-input behavior is required.

Implement reward_delivery_selection(arg). Arg additionally has vehicle and budget, an integer from 0 to 100. Each request also has reward. Choose any subset of requests and serve exactly that subset with the vehicle on a feasible route costing at most budget inclusive. Return the greatest total reward of served requests, an integer. If no subset has a feasible route within budget, return 0; zero is also the value of any feasible empty subset. Reward is earned only after both events complete. There is no secondary cost or request-count objective.

The function takes one dictionary a and must not mutate it. All numbers are exact integers (not booleans). Keys are n, edges, start, goal, state, delta, accept, budget; budget_route_strategy additionally has owners. There are no other keys.

n is 1..8. start and goal are vertex indices 0..n-1. delta is a rectangular list with 1..5 rows and 1..3 columns, each entry a state index 0..len(delta)-1; state is an initial state index. accept is a list of distinct state indices, possibly empty.

edges is a list of 0..20 lists [source, destination, label, resource, cost]. Vertices are in 0..n-1, label is a column index in delta, resource is 1..8, cost is -20..20. budget is 0..24. Parallel entries, self loops, and repeated entries are legal.

A walk starts at start in state with resource use zero and cost zero. Taking an edge at the current vertex adds its resource and cost, moves to its destination, and replaces state q by delta[q][label]. Total resource may not exceed budget. An accepted ending has vertex goal and state in accept. The empty walk is allowed. Reaching an accepted ending does not prevent taking further edges.

Return a list of budget+1 integers. Entry b is the number of accepted walks with total resource exactly b, modulo 1000000007. Walks are distinguished by their ordered sequence of indices in edges, so repeated equal entries are distinct choices. Edge costs do not affect counts.

The function takes one dictionary a and must not mutate it. All numbers are exact integers (not booleans). Keys are n, edges, start, goal, state, delta, accept, budget; budget_route_strategy additionally has owners. There are no other keys.

n is 1..8. start and goal are vertex indices 0..n-1. delta is a rectangular list with 1..5 rows and 1..3 columns, each entry a state index 0..len(delta)-1; state is an initial state index. accept is a list of distinct state indices, possibly empty.

edges is a list of 0..20 lists [source, destination, label, resource, cost]. Vertices are in 0..n-1, label is a column index in delta, resource is 1..8, cost is -20..20. budget is 0..24. Parallel entries, self loops, and repeated entries are legal.

A walk starts at start in state with resource use zero and cost zero. Taking an edge at the current vertex adds its resource and cost, moves to its destination, and replaces state q by delta[q][label]. Total resource may not exceed budget. An accepted ending has vertex goal and state in accept. The empty walk is allowed. Reaching an accepted ending does not prevent taking further edges.

owners is a list of n integers, each 0 or 1. At a vertex owned by 0 the minimizing player chooses an action; at a vertex owned by 1 the adversary chooses an action. Both observe the complete history. Legal actions are taking any outgoing edge whose resource fits the remaining budget, and stopping if and only if the current ending is accepted. Stopping ends successfully with no additional cost. There is no stop action elsewhere.

If there are no legal actions play ends unsuccessfully. All plays are finite because every edge spends positive resource. A strategy guarantees success only if every adversarial choice leads to successful stopping. Return None if the minimizing player has no strategy guaranteeing success; otherwise return the least possible worst-case total cost among its success-guaranteeing strategies, as an integer. At an adversarial accepted ending the adversary may choose an edge instead of stopping.

The function takes one dictionary a and must not mutate it. Integer fields contain exact integers, not booleans. alphabet is a list of 1..3 distinct strings, each exactly one Unicode code point. All text strings contain only characters in alphabet. String lengths count Unicode code points.

delta is a rectangular list of 1..5 rows and len(alphabet) columns containing state indices 0..len(delta)-1. state is an initial state index. accept is a list of distinct state indices, possibly empty. An output is accepted when starting at state and replacing q with delta[q][alphabet.index(c)] for each output character c leaves q in accept. The empty output is tested at state.
max_output is an integer 0..12. Only outputs of length at most max_output are permitted.

The exact keys are alphabet, delta, state, accept, max_output, text, mode, next_mode, cost, max_ops. text has length 0..12. next_mode is a list of 1..4 rows of three mode indices. cost has the same dimensions with each entry an integer 1..20. mode is an initial mode index. max_ops is an integer 0..24.

A script reads text once from left to right and emits its output from left to right. Operation index 0 inserts any one alphabet character without consuming input. Operation index 1 deletes the next input character and emits nothing. Operation index 2 consumes the next input character and emits any one alphabet character, including the identical character. Delete and substitute require an unconsumed input character. There is no free copy operation.

Each operation at mode m adds cost[m][operation] and then sets the mode to next_mode[m][operation]. Character choice does not affect this mode update or cost. The initial cost is zero. A successful script consumes all of text, emits an accepted output, and uses at most max_ops operations. It may continue inserting after consuming all input. The empty script is allowed. No acceptance condition is imposed on the final edit mode.

Return the number of successful scripts of globally minimum total cost, modulo 1000000007, as an integer. Return 0 if none exist. A script is its ordered sequence of operation indices and emitted characters (deletion has no emitted character). Different sequences count separately, even when their output, cost, consumed characters, or final mode coincide. The operation limit applies before minimizing cost; scripts of any length from zero through max_ops compete together.

The function takes one dictionary a and must not mutate it. Integer fields contain exact integers, not booleans. alphabet is a list of 1..3 distinct strings, each exactly one Unicode code point. All text strings contain only characters in alphabet. String lengths count Unicode code points.

delta is a rectangular list of 1..5 rows and len(alphabet) columns containing state indices 0..len(delta)-1. state is an initial state index. accept is a list of distinct state indices, possibly empty. An output is accepted when starting at state and replacing q with delta[q][alphabet.index(c)] for each output character c leaves q in accept. The empty output is tested at state.
max_output is an integer 0..12. Only outputs of length at most max_output are permitted.
The exact keys are alphabet, delta, state, accept, max_output, left, right. left and right are strings of length 0..12.

For strings x and y, their Levenshtein distance is the smallest number of unit-cost single-character insertions, deletions, and substitutions transforming x to y. Identical characters may be retained for zero cost. There are no edit modes or operation-count limits.

Return the minimum of distance(left,output)+distance(right,output) over all permitted accepted outputs as an integer, or None if no permitted accepted output exists. Both distances use the same output, and each is minimized independently.
